To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the finite-$t$, target mass and target radius corrections are large, of the order of $20\%$ or larger, and must be taken in account in the analysis of DVCS experiments.

the finite-$t$, target mass and target mass dependent finite-$t$ power corrections are significant and should be taken into account when analyzing the DVCS data in order to extract the generalized parton distributions.
the finite-$t$, finite-$m^2$ and finite-$\epsilon$ corrections to the DVCS observables are significant at the intermediate photon virtualities and should be accounted for.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the calculation of the twist-four corrections to the DVCS cross section in the framework of the collinear factorization.
a complete calculation of power corrections to DVCS at the twist four level.
the theoretical description of DVCS at the twist-4 accuracy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the leading twist approximation for DVCS is not applicable at $Q^2 \lesssim 1$-$2$ GeV$^2$.
the DVCS cross-section at the leading twist is not convention independent, and the higher-twist corrections are not small.
the leading twist approximation to DVCS is not sufficient for the kinematic range of $Q^2 \sim 1$ - $5$ GeV$^2$ and $-t \sim 1-5$ GeV $^2$.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the leading twist approximation in DVCS is not sufficient to describe the existing data at $Q^2<5\,{\text{GeV}^2}$ and the finite-$t$, target mass and higher twist corrections are of comparable importance to the leading twist terms.
DVCS is an important process for the study of higher twist physics.
the leading twist approximation to DVCS is valid only for $Q^2>5\,{\mathrm{GeV}}^2$, while the higher twist effects are important for $Q^1\,{\mathrm{-}}\,5\,{\textrm{GeV}}^ 2$.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the twist-four corrections are not large and can be reliably estimated within the framework of QCD.
the twist-four corrections are under control at the level of a few percent.
the higher-twist effects are not negligible in this kinematic region and should not be omitted from the theoretical description.
